fields.name: Banwārīlāl Siṁha (Pāñcthupi)
fields.disappearance: Phālguna śukla tṛtīyā, 1313 BS (1906) (the record's text)
fields.notes: Of an Uttara-rāḍhīya kāyastha family of Pāñcthupi (born 1838); woken to renunciation by Kṛṣṇadayāla, a kīrtanīyā of the Manoharaśāhī school; founded Śrī Harivāsara at his home, a shelter for renounced Vaiṣṇavas of Vraja, Purī and Gauḍa. Tribhaṅga dāsa Bābājī (#1555) served there; his son Vijayakiśora Siṁha kept it after him. Died 1906 (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Jīvana 333). (The guru field said «Krishnadayala»: the text says only that his company woke him to renunciation.)

fields.appearance: Probably the 1730s (a land grant from King Kṛṣṇacandra is dated 1167 BS, 1762: the record's text)
fields.notes: Seventh in descent from Advaita Prabhu; the foremost paṇḍita of Śāntipura, famed for his works on Smṛti and Navya-nyāya; King Kṛṣṇacandra of Navadvīpa gave him land in 1762. Wrote many works on Vaiṣṇava theology and practice, among them a ṭippanī on the Tattva-sandarbha.

fields.guru: His father Trivikrama Tīrtha, disciple of Madhvācārya
fields.works: Madhva-vijaya; Madhva-vijaya-bhāva-prakāśikā; some twenty books in all
fields.notes: Youngest son of Trivikrama Ācārya (Trivikrama Tīrtha), Madhvācārya's disciple; of Viṣṇumaṅgala; author of the Madhva-vijaya, from his father's diary of Madhva's life; spent some thirty years among Madhva and his disciples. His younger brother became Viṣṇu Tīrtha (CC Madhya 9.245 p).
